overview: Extends the Phase 1 Layercake membership solution so that every membership event (Join, Change, Lapse, Readmission, Renewal) can be segmented by payment method, payer type and concession type, every Join, Renewal and Readmission can carry its contact-year's invoiced amount in GBP, and Practising / Retired is set from a retirement date derived from retired concessions (AMD-001). Subscription invoices, invoice lines, corporate subscriptions and the concession reference are landed 1:1 in bronze from objects other systems own, and the Phase 1 brnz_subs_status gains 'Inv Total Amount' and 'Retired Concession' from Subs.vwSubsMemberStatuses. Invoice lines are landed at the source's ledger-distribution grain, one row per (recid, postingtype, accountdisplayvalue), and every reader takes a transaction's settled amount once per transaction (AMD-002, ADR-006). Silver adds the segment reference lists, an item-code line-type mapping, a currency list and one attributes row per contact per Campaign Year, set from each year's segment invoice. It adds silv_event_amount, which places each contact-year's Inv Total Amount on one event and pairs each event with its own eligible invoice for the invoice checks only, and ten new anomaly types in the existing silv_data_anomaly. A new view derives each contact's retirement date from brnz_subs_status, and the Phase 1 silv_member_base load takes it in place of apuk_retirementdate (ADR-005), so in Phase 1 only results split by membership status change. Four new gold dimensions are added, and the existing silver and gold event tables carry the segment keys, carried flags, subs_amount_gbp, invoiced_subtotal_gbp and amount_status. The daily load is made accurate (AMD-003). On every run, the Phase 1 daily count finds the past dates whose silver inputs changed by comparing the inputs with a stored basis (ADR-007). It recomputes them from 2020-10-01 onward and writes only the differences, so stored daily history always equals a full rebuild. Each change to a date already loaded is recorded in the new Layercake.silv_daily_count_adjustment. Two table functions give the figures as known at any time, and a view lists the adjustments for review (ADR-008). Layercake.usp_run_daily_load now ends by running the segment loads (usp_run_payment_segments, ADR-001) under the same run_id, so one call populates everything. Count-only profiling, coverage, retirement and employer findings queries are delivered as read-only procedures (ADR-003). Employer segmentation is findings only, so no employer objects are created. Every change ships as a framework migration with a tested down script, all objects live in the Layercake schema, and names follow the Phase 1 conventions.

layers.name: bronze
layers.purpose: brnz_* tables: 1:1 landings of external sources (Subs.tblSubsInvoices, synapse_fo.CUSTTRANS_RICS at its ledger-distribution grain, Subs.vwCorpSubscriptions, CE.vwConcessionType) with the standard bronze audit columns and soft delete, and the Phase 1 brnz_subs_status (Subs.vwSubsMemberStatuses) extended with inv_total_amount and retired_concession. No value transformation and no aggregation.

layers.name: silver
layers.purpose: silv_* tables and views: segment reference lists with reserved ids, the line-type mapping, the currency list, the eligible-invoice view, silv_member_year_attributes, silv_event_amount, the derived retirement date view, the new columns on the existing silv_membership_events, anomaly rows in the existing silv_data_anomaly, and the derived date held in the existing silv_member_base.retirement_date. The Phase 1 daily counts (silv_daily_count_detail, silv_daily_count) are corrected for every changed past date on every run. silv_daily_count_adjustment holds their adjustment history, read through the as-known-at functions and the adjustments review view.

layers.name: gold
layers.purpose: dim_payment_method, dim_payer_type, dim_currency and dim_concession_type copied from silver, and the new keys, flags and GBP amount measures on the existing fact_membership_events. fact_daily_member_count_detail and fact_annual_rate_base keep their grain and columns (Q-007); only their Practising / Retired split changes, through the unchanged Phase 1 loads (REQ-017).

layers.name: reporting queries
layers.purpose: usp_profile_* and usp_report_* read-only procedures that return aggregates only (counts, sums, rates) for profiling, coverage, retirement comparison and employer findings.

layers.name: load logging
layers.purpose: Every load records start, row counts and outcome in Layercake.etl_run_log through the existing Layercake.usp_etl_log_start and Layercake.usp_etl_log_end (project override of base standards 3). The Phase 1 daily count control tables etl_daily_count_loaded and etl_daily_count_pending_rebuild stay; the pending-rebuild table becomes a diagnostic only. etl_daily_count_input_basis is added to hold the daily count's silver inputs as last applied (ADR-007).

entities.name: Layercake.usp_load_brnz_subs_invoice_line
entities.description: Lands the RULE-077 scope of synapse_fo.CUSTTRANS_RICS into brnz_subs_invoice_line at the source's grain, one row per source row (RULE-104). MOD-019 changes it to match source rows to bronze on (recid, postingtype, accountdisplayvalue). A null matches a null, and strings are compared under the database collation, as the unique index compares them. It inserts new rows; updates rows whose values differ, including the five ledger columns, and refreshes _updated_at; soft-deletes rows gone from the source; and restores rows that reappear. Unchanged rows are untouched, so a rerun on unchanged source logs 0 inserted, 0 updated and 0 deleted, and a change to one row of a split transaction updates that row only. Two source rows in scope with the same identity fail the load: it logs Failed, re-raises and leaves the target unchanged, and no row is skipped. The row-count check (live rows equal the source rows in scope) and the logging are unchanged. Rows landed before the change hold null in the new columns, so the first run after deployment soft-deletes them and inserts the source rows at the new grain. The exception is a source row whose postingtype and accountdisplayvalue are also both null: that row matches its old row and is updated. The down script restores the MOD-002 definition.

Never reads invoice or line amounts. Writes only differences: new events inserted, changed rows updated, rows for events that no longer exist deleted. Logged.

entities.name: Layercake.usp_load_silv_data_anomaly_invoice
entities.description: Derives the six invoice anomaly types from the match held in silv_event_amount (invoice_rec_id, match_outcome) and from vw_silv_eligible_invoice, for amount Campaign Years from 2022 only (RULE-093), and reconciles them with silv_data_anomaly as the segment anomaly load does. The readmission checks look for a 'readmission fee' line among the matched invoice's own lines in brnz_subs_invoice_line, typed through silv_ref_invoice_line_type; they never read the event amount (RULE-044, Q-042). anomaly_nk is the event_nk for event-level types and the invoice rec_id for invoice-level types. It touches only its own six types. Logged.

entities.name: Layercake.usp_load_silv_membership_events_segments
entities.description: Writes the new columns on silv_membership_events (ADR-001). Keys and carried flags come from the silv_member_year_attributes row for the contact and the event's segment Campaign Year (RULE-017), or 0 where there is no row. Join, Renewal and Readmission take subs_amount_gbp, invoiced_subtotal_gbp and amount_status from silv_event_amount by event_nk; Change and Lapse get nulls. Updates only rows whose new-column values differ. Never inserts or deletes events, and never touches Phase 1 columns. Logged.

entities.name: Layercake.usp_load_fact_membership_events_segments
entities.description: Copies the new columns from silv_membership_events onto fact_membership_events by event_id, updating only rows that differ. It then runs the extended silver-to-gold check: equal row counts by payment_method_id, equal counts by amount_status, and equal sums of subs_amount_gbp and invoiced_subtotal_gbp (RULE-019, AC-008-11). A failed check fails the load. Logged.

entities.name: Layercake.usp_run_payment_segments
entities.description: Runs the solution's loads in dependency order after the Phase 1 run: bronze loads; the line-type and currency lists and concession reference; the gold dimensions; member-year attributes; event amounts; the segment and invoice anomalies; the silver event columns; the gold fact columns. It stops at the first failure, which that load has already logged, and re-raises it. Since MOD-023 it is called by Layercake.usp_run_daily_load as that run's last step, under the daily run's run_id, so nobody schedules it. It stays callable on its own for a segment-only rerun (RULE-126). Its own definition is unchanged.

entities.name: Layercake.usp_profile_custtrans_grain
entities.description: Count-only grain profile of synapse_fo.CUSTTRANS_RICS (RULE-095). It takes invoice rows (TRANSTYPE not 8 or 24, invoice number containing neither 'CRE' nor 'FTCN'), groups them by ACCOUNTNUM and INVOICE, and returns the number of invoices by rows per invoice, by distinct productcode per invoice, and by whether the invoice has a sales tax row. It reads the external source directly, so it can run before the invoice build.

entities.name: Layercake.usp_profile_corp_subscription_status
entities.description: Row counts of Subs.vwCorpSubscriptions by 'Sub Status' value and by 'Sub User Status' value (RULE-096). Settles the active value assumed under Q-027.

entities.name: Layercake.usp_report_retirement_comparison
entities.description: For each Campaign Year, over paid positions: counts with a retired concession (the year's concession type has one of the six retired item codes, Q-018) and a derived retirement date (vw_silv_derived_retirement_date) on or before campaign_year_end; retired concession only; derived date only; neither; and the agreement rate (RULE-055 to RULE-057). apuk_retirementdate plays no part (RULE-058). entities.name: Layercake.usp_report_employer_scheme_coverage

entities.name: Layercake.usp_report_top_employers

entities.name: Layercake.usp_report_payment_method_coverage

entities.name: Layercake.usp_report_invoiced_subtotal_coverage

entities.name: Layercake.usp_load_silv_data_anomaly

entities.name: Layercake.vw_silv_derived_retirement_date

entities.name: Layercake.silv_daily_count_adjustment
entities.description: Adjustment history of the daily counts (REQ-019). There is one row per daily count cell per run that changed any of the cell's seven measures. The cell is the grain of silv_daily_count_detail: [date], region, country_id, gender_id, grade and membership_status_id. Each row holds new minus old for each measure. A cell missing on either side counts as 0 (RULE-113). A measure the run did not change holds 0, and a check constraint rejects a row whose seven changes are all 0. The first load of a date never loaded before writes no row. Every later change writes one: repeat loads of today, corrections of past dates, and manual @RebuildFrom and @FullRebuild calls (RULE-114, RULE-115). Rows are written in the same transaction as the change they record, so a rolled-back change leaves no row (RULE-116). The table is insert-only: no load updates or deletes a row, and nothing purges it (RULE-117). grade holds the silver grades ('enrolment', 'election', 'lapse'), as silv_daily_count_detail does. Unique on (run_id, [date], region, country_id, gender_id, grade, membership_status_id).

columns.description: Identity; technical key in write order. Clustered.

columns.description: When the row was written, in database server local time, the clock etl_run_log uses (Q-049). Rows written in one batch share one time.

columns.name: date
columns.description: The changed cell's date

columns.name: grade

columns.description: New minus old active_count; 0 where unchanged

entities.name: Layercake.fn_silv_daily_count_detail_as_known_at
entities.description: Table function giving the daily counts as known at a time, at the detail grain (ADR-008, RULE-119 to RULE-121). Parameters: @date_from date and @date_to date, both inclusive, and @as_known_at datetime2(3). If any parameter is NULL, no rows are returned. It returns one row per detail cell in the date range that has a stored row in silv_daily_count_detail or an adjustment written after @as_known_at. Each of the seven figures is the stored figure (0 where the cell has no stored row) minus the sum of that cell's changes in silv_daily_count_adjustment written strictly after @as_known_at. A change written exactly at @as_known_at is part of the figure (Q-049). A cell with no stored row whose seven figures all come to 0 is not returned. A date first loaded after @as_known_at returns its first-load figures (Q-050). With @as_known_at after the latest adjustment, it returns exactly the stored rows.

entities.name: Layercake.fn_silv_daily_count_as_known_at
entities.description: Table function giving the daily counts as known at a time, at the silv_daily_count grain (ADR-008, RULE-120). It returns one row per [date], region and grade that the detail function returns, with the detail figures summed over country_id, gender_id and membership_status_id. With @as_known_at after the latest adjustment, it equals silv_daily_count on these columns (AC-020-03, AC-020-09).

entities.name: Layercake.vw_silv_daily_count_adjustment_review
entities.description: The adjustments for review (RULE-122, Q-051): one row per silv_daily_count_adjustment row and measure whose change is not 0. Each row carries the cell's grain columns, the run, the time written, the measure name and the change. Rows are not summed to date level, so changes that cancel out across cells (for example Practising -1, Retired +1) stay visible.

columns.name: change_value

It holds one row per contact with daily count inputs (input_name 'contact', input_key = contact_no). It also holds one row per reference table the Phase 1 daily derivation reads (input_name = the table name, input_key empty). The fingerprint covers only the rows and columns the derivation reads. Changes to segment and amount columns on events, and to load audit columns, are therefore not input changes (AC-019-08). For ref_date_spine and ref_campaign_year_config it covers only the rows up to the latest loaded date, so the daily extension of the spine is not a change. Only usp_load_silv_daily_count writes the table, and only after every corrected date of the run has committed: changed rows are updated, new ones inserted, and rows whose input has gone are deleted. The table is empty after deployment, so the first run recomputes every date from 2020-10-01 (RULE-109).

entities.name: Layercake.silv_daily_count_detail
entities.description: Existing Phase 1 silver daily counts: one row per [date], region, country_id, gender_id, grade and membership_status_id, with campaign_year, campaign_quarter and the seven measures active_count, paid_count, paid_count_event, event_join_count, event_renewal_count, event_readmission_count and event_lapse_count. Structure unchanged; no change script. MOD-022 changes how its rows are written. They are written only where the figures differ, and each change to a date already loaded is recorded in silv_daily_count_adjustment. Every changed past date from 2020-10-01 is corrected on every run (REQ-018). grade holds 'enrolment', 'election' or 'lapse'. The gold fact_daily_member_count_detail follows it through the unchanged Phase 1 gold load.

entities.name: Layercake.silv_daily_count
entities.description: Existing Phase 1 silver daily counts at the [date], region and grade grain, with campaign_year, campaign_quarter and the seven measures. Structure unchanged; no change script. It is written with the detail table: only where figures differ, and for every corrected date (REQ-018). It holds the detail figures summed over country_id, gender_id and membership_status_id (assumed under Q-052). Its changes are therefore not recorded separately: they are the sums of the detail adjustments.

entities.name: Layercake.usp_load_silv_daily_count
entities.description: Existing Phase 1 daily count load, called by usp_load_silver in the silver step after the member profile. MOD-022 changes it; the derivation of a date's cells is unchanged. What changes is which dates it recomputes and how it writes them (daily count correction and adjustment history patterns). Every run compares the inputs with etl_daily_count_input_basis, finds the earliest affected date (ADR-007) and recomputes every date from there to today. That includes today, which is recomputed on every run, and dates not yet loaded. @RebuildFrom and @FullRebuild can only move that start earlier. Dates are recomputed in date-ordered batches and written as differences only, with unchanged rows left untouched. Each batch commits in one transaction with its etl_daily_count_loaded marks and one silv_daily_count_adjustment row per changed detail cell of a date already marked loaded. The basis is advanced only after the last batch commits, so the next run completes a failed one with no cleanup. The load also marks open etl_daily_count_pending_rebuild rows applied once its correction covers their affected_from. Its signature, parameters and logging step are unchanged. The down script restores the Phase 1 definition.

entities.name: Layercake.usp_run_daily_load
entities.description: Existing Phase 1 daily run: bronze, silver and gold steps under one run_id, with its own 'run' row in etl_run_log. MOD-023 changes it in one respect only. After the gold step, it runs Layercake.usp_run_payment_segments with the same run_id and no as-of date, so the attributes load uses the run date and one call populates Phase 1 and every segment column (RULE-123, RULE-124). It opens no transaction of its own, as today. A failure in any step, Phase 1 or segment, logs its run row 'Failed' and re-raises the original error to the caller. Steps that committed before the failure stay committed, and running it again recovers (RULE-125). Its parameters, its logging and the Phase 1 steps are unchanged. The down script restores the Phase 1 definition.

patterns: Run order (ADR-001, REQ-021): Layercake.usp_run_daily_load runs the Phase 1 bronze, silver and gold steps. As its last step, it runs Layercake.usp_run_payment_segments under the same run_id and with no as-of date. Every Phase 1 table the segment loads read or write onto (silv_membership_events, fact_membership_events, silv_payment_events, brnz_subs_status) is therefore current before they run, and the run ends with every segment column populated (RULE-124). Nobody schedules a second procedure, and usp_run_payment_segments can still be run alone for a segment-only rerun (RULE-126). The run opens no transaction of its own. Each load commits on its own, a failure in any load fails the run and is re-raised to the caller, and running it again recovers (RULE-125). Phase 1 procedures that change: the silv_payment_events load stops writing payment_source; usp_load_silv_data_anomaly resolves only its own types; usp_load_brnz_subs_status lands two more columns; usp_load_silv_member_base takes the derived retirement date (ADR-005); usp_load_silv_daily_count corrects every changed past date and records adjustments (ADR-007); and usp_run_daily_load gains the segment step. The member status and member base loads run inside the Phase 1 run, bronze before silver, so the derived date is current before any Phase 1 status is set. The daily count runs after them in the silver step, so a changed retirement date reaches past daily counts in the same run.

Bronze (REQ-002, REQ-006, REQ-010): full comparison with the source on its key on every run. New rows are inserted with _loaded_at and _updated_at set. Changed rows are updated and _updated_at refreshed. Rows missing from the source get _is_deleted = 1 and _deleted_at; rows that reappear are restored. Unchanged rows are untouched, so a rerun on unchanged source logs 0 inserted, 0 updated and 0 deleted. Values are never transformed or defaulted. Each load checks that live rows equal the source rows in scope and fails if not (RULE-004, RULE-005). String columns take the database's default collation, so they compare with Phase 1 columns without collation conflicts. The Phase 1 brnz_subs_status keeps its own load's behaviour; its two new columns take part in that load's change test (RULE-103).

Reference lists: payment method and payer type are static lists seeded by their migrations. Concession type is insert-and-update by business key. Line type and currency are insert-only. Ids never change between loads. Reserved ids 0 Unknown, -1 Unrecognised and -2 Not applicable have the same labels in all three segment lists (RULE-078). Each gold dimension mirrors its silver list by id. Line types serve the eligible-invoice test and the readmission fee check only, and the currency list describes no event amount (RULE-030, Q-038).

Eligible and segment invoice (RULE-014, RULE-079): eligibility is defined once in vw_silv_eligible_invoice and used by both the attributes load and the invoice match in the event amount load. The latest eligible invoice by trans_date is the segment invoice. Ties on trans_date go to the higher rec_id (Q-036).

Attributes, all segments: contact-years before 2022 get -2 Not applicable for payment method, payer type and concession, with every carried flag 0 (RULE-080, Q-011). Years from 2022 with no eligible invoice carry forward from the latest earlier year that has one: always for payment method and payer type, and for concession only when that type is perpetual. A carried value gets carried flag 1. Where nothing can be carried, the value is 0 Unknown with flag 0 (RULE-016, RULE-023, RULE-051, Q-006).

Attributes, payment method (RULE-012 to RULE-015, RULE-105): the segment invoice's inv_payment_method, mapped by fn_map_payment_method. Only when that is null or blank do the payment lines decide. Payment lines are the live brnz_subs_invoice_line rows with lastsettlevoucher equal to the invoice voucher and accountnum equal to its account_num, with a non-blank paymmode. Each payment transaction (recid) counts once, however many lines it is split into. Its mapped payment mode, its transdate and the absolute value of its settleamountcur (null counts as 0) are customer-transaction values that the owner's source repeats on every row of the recid. They are taken once per recid and never summed across its rows. The method with the largest total settled amount wins. On a tie, the method whose earliest payment is earliest wins, then the lowest recid. With no qualifying payment line, the value is 0 Unknown with flag 0. A non-blank invoice code the mapping does not know gives -1 Unrecognised, with no fallback.

Attributes, payer type (RULE-020 to RULE-024, RULE-082, RULE-083): a live corporate subscription for a year is a live brnz_corporate_subscription row for the contact with sub_campaign_year equal to that year and both sub_status and sub_user_status active. The active value is 'Active' (Q-027), held in one place in the load. Corporate when the segment invoice's method is Corporate and a live subscription exists. On a double payment (the segment invoice settled both by Corporate and by another method), Corporate where a live subscription exists, otherwise Individual (RULE-026). Otherwise Individual where the contact has a Phase 1 paid position that year, else 0 Unknown. corporate_account_ref is the live subscription's scheme_no for Corporate years (if there are several, the lowest scheme_no, Q-036), is carried with a carried Corporate payer type, and is null otherwise (Q-019).

Attributes, concession (RULE-049 to RULE-052): the segment invoice's lines with item codes starting 'CON' are matched to silv_ref_concession_type.item_code. Where there are several, the one with the highest discount (apuk_discount through the business key) wins. A code not in the reference gives -1 Unrecognised. No concession line gives No concession.

Event amounts (RULE-032, RULE-033, RULE-035, RULE-038, RULE-040, RULE-041, RULE-098; Q-038, Q-039, Q-044, Q-047): each Join, Renewal and Readmission has an amount Campaign Year: its own year for Renewal and Readmission; for a Join, its contact's first paid position's year, else its own year (Q-029). Within each contact and amount Campaign Year exactly one event carries the amount: Readmission before Renewal before Join, then the earliest event_date, then the lowest event_id. That event takes inv_total_amount from the live brnz_subs_status row (_is_deleted = 0) with the same contact number and Campaign Year as invoiced_subtotal_gbp, and subs_amount_gbp holds the same value. A Full Concession year carries the source amount (0.00 where the source gives 0), never null. Amounts are null on the other events, where the amount Campaign Year is before 2022, where there is no live status row, and where inv_total_amount is null. The value is held in the events' existing decimal(19,4) columns. No amount is ever taken from brnz_subs_invoice or brnz_subs_invoice_line, so changing an invoice or line amount changes no event amount (AC-008-27). Firm-level corporate discounts are not spread to individuals (Q-005, known gap).

amount_status (RULE-088, Q-045): every Join, Renewal and Readmission gets exactly one value, the first that applies: 'Before invoice data' (amount Campaign Year before 2022); 'No invoice' (no live status row, or its inv_total_amount is null); 'Counted on another event' (another event in the contact and amount Campaign Year carries the amount); 'Full Concession' (Member Invoice Position 'Full Concession'); 'Fully credited' (Member Invoice Position 'Fully Credited'); otherwise 'Invoiced', which covers every other position. 'Unmapped lines' is retired, and a check constraint on silv_event_amount admits only the six values. Change and Lapse get null.

Invoice match for the checks (RULE-084 to RULE-086, RULE-089; ADR-002; Q-042): used only by the REQ-009 anomalies, never for amounts. For each contact and amount Campaign Year from 2022, events are ordered by event date and eligible invoices by trans_date (ties by event_nk and rec_id, Q-036). Equal counts pair in order. With more events than invoices, the invoices go to events in the order Readmission, Renewal, Join, earliest event date; the chosen events are paired with the invoices by date, and the rest get match outcome Invoice shortfall. With more invoices than events, the events are paired by date with the latest invoices, and the earlier surplus invoices go unmatched. No invoice is matched to two events.

Event columns (RULE-017, RULE-018, RULE-081): an event's segment Campaign Year is its own year, except a Join, which uses its amount Campaign Year. The keys and the three carried flags come from that attributes row, or 0 where there is none. Gold copies silver by event_id.

Anomalies: each new procedure owns a fixed set of anomaly types and reconciles them on every run. It inserts cases newly raised, deletes cases no longer raised (for example after a corrected invoice) and leaves existing cases untouched, so a rerun on unchanged data changes no anomaly rows. anomaly_nk identifies the event, the invoice or the contact-year. Invoice anomalies are raised only for amount Campaign Years from 2022 (RULE-093). Each Readmission with an amount Campaign Year from 2022 that has no matched invoice, or whose matched invoice has no own line of line type 'readmission fee', gets exactly one row: EVENT_NO_INVOICE or INVOICE_MATCHES_MULTIPLE_EVENTS where it has no invoice; READMISSION_FREE where its event date falls in the free-readmission window (Campaign Year quarter 2, ADR-004, Q-032); READMISSION_NO_FEE otherwise. The event amount plays no part (AC-009-10).

Derived retirement date (RULE-099 to RULE-102, ADR-005): vw_silv_derived_retirement_date gives each contact the Renewal Date of its earliest live brnz_subs_status Campaign Year with retired_concession 'Retired Conc.' and a Renewal Date. usp_load_silv_member_base writes it to silv_member_base.retirement_date, null where there is none, with no fallback to apuk_retirementdate or 'First Retired Year' (Q-040). The Phase 1 status rule is unchanged: a contact is Retired from that date, inclusive. The events load and the annual rate base read it directly and correct themselves on the next run; the daily count reads the copy in silv_member_profile. Only membership_status_id and results split by it change; totals across statuses, event rows and event identifiers do not (Q-046). Tests that need an apuk_retirementdate set it on the Phase 1 source (brnz_rics_record), and before-and-after comparisons compare with a snapshot taken before the change (AC-017-07).

Daily count correction (REQ-018, RULE-106 to RULE-111, ADR-007): the Phase 1 derivation of a date's cells is unchanged; usp_load_silv_daily_count changes which dates it recomputes and how it writes them. (1) Start date. Each run compares the current silver inputs with etl_daily_count_input_basis. A contact's inputs are its rows in silv_membership_events, silv_member_state_ranges, silv_payment_events and silv_member_profile, limited to the columns the derivation reads. Each other table the derivation reads (for example ref_date_spine, ref_campaign_year_config and the grade and status lists) is one reference input, and the spine and Campaign Year list are compared only over dates already loaded. A contact whose inputs changed, appeared or disappeared contributes the earliest date its old or new rows can affect: the start of the Campaign Year of its earliest input row, never before 2020-10-01. The earliest input row is taken over event dates, range starts, payment and renewal dates and the Campaign Years the rows refer to. A changed reference input contributes 2020-10-01. The run's start is the earliest of these, the first date not yet loaded, and today. @RebuildFrom (or 2020-10-01 for @FullRebuild) can only move it earlier. (2) Recompute and write. Every date from the start to today is recomputed in date-ordered batches. For each date, in silv_daily_count_detail and silv_daily_count, cells newly derived are inserted, cells whose figures differ are updated, and cells no longer derived are deleted. Unchanged rows are untouched. Each batch commits in one transaction with its adjustment rows and its etl_daily_count_loaded marks. (3) Basis. After the last batch commits, the basis is brought into line with the inputs the run used, in its own transaction. (4) Failure. A run that fails part way keeps its committed batches and re-raises the error. The basis is unchanged, so the next run starts at the same date or earlier, finds no differences in the batches already corrected and finishes the rest, with no cleanup (RULE-111). (5) First run after deployment. The basis is empty, so the run recomputes every date from 2020-10-01 and corrects the drift so far (RULE-109). This replaces the ASM-002 one-off @RebuildFrom, which ADR-005's consequences described, and no person runs a rebuild after deployment. (6) etl_daily_count_pending_rebuild stays as a diagnostic. Its producers are unchanged and still log to it, and the daily count marks open rows applied once a run's correction covers their affected_from. Nothing reads it to decide what to recompute (RULE-110). (7) fact_daily_member_count_detail is unchanged: its Phase 1 load already applies differences across the whole span, so gold follows silver in the same run. After any completed run the stored history equals @FullRebuild on the same data, for all seven measures and every Campaign Year from 2020-10-01, closed or not (RULE-107, RULE-108). A run takes longer when the earliest change reaches far back.

Idempotency and corrections: every load recomputes from current sources and writes only differences, so reruns change nothing, and late or corrected source rows flow through on the next run. From AMD-003 this includes the daily counts for every past date (ADR-007). Audit columns change only when a row's values change. No type 2 history is kept: silver and gold reflect the current sources and bronze keeps soft-delete flags. The one history table is the daily count adjustment history (REQ-019).

Error handling and logging: each load procedure follows base standards 3 (try/catch with XACT_ABORT, the error recorded, then re-raised). It logs start, rows inserted, updated and deleted, and outcome through Layercake.usp_etl_log_start and Layercake.usp_etl_log_end, with the start logged before the load's transaction.

Deployment: one migration per module (MIG-0003 onward), each with a down script. Changes to existing Layercake tables go through change scripts that the down script reverses exactly. Down scripts restore the previous definitions of changed code objects and rename new tables that hold rows to <table>_rolledback_MIGnnnn. The eight event amount columns dropped under Q-038 hold only nulls, and their down script adds them back. No external object is created, altered or written to (RULE-076).

Spec questions this design depends on: Q-001 (payment method source) for attributes; Q-002, Q-019 and Q-027 for payer type, corporate_account_ref and the corporate anomalies; Q-005 for corporate amounts (known gap); Q-006 for carry-forward; Q-007 for leaving the daily and annual tables' grain unchanged; Q-008 for brnz_concession's source; Q-011 for pre-2022 handling; Q-012 for the segment invoice; Q-015 for no Mixed value; Q-017 for the subtotal-below-standard-rate check; Q-018 for the retired codes in the comparison; Q-024 for removing payment_source; Q-028 for Phase 1 column names; Q-029 for Joins with no paid position; Q-010 for the employer findings. Q-021 is answered (AMD-002): invoice lines are at ledger-distribution grain, and the rules that depended on it keep synapse_fo.CUSTTRANS_RICS as their source, read as the invoice line grain pattern describes. Each assumption sits in one rule of one load, so an answer changes one procedure. Q-049, Q-050 and Q-051 are answered (AMD-003). They fix the as-known-at boundary (only changes written strictly after T are subtracted, in server local time), the first-load figures for dates loaded after T, and the review view's cell grain. Each is held in one function or view.

Invoice line grain (RULE-104, RULE-105; Q-021, AMD-002): brnz_subs_invoice_line holds one row per ledger distribution, so one customer transaction (recid) can have several rows, for example one per cost centre or Campaign Year. Every reader follows two rules. First, a line's own amounts (amountcur, amountmst) belong to the row, while transaction-level values repeat on every row of a recid. settleamountcur is the one landed; CustTrans_AmountCur and CustTrans_AmountMst are not landed. Transaction-level values are taken once per recid and never summed across its rows. Second, counts of transactions or invoices count distinct recids or invoices, never rows. How each reader meets this. The line-type mapping adds one row per distinct (productcode, ricinvoicetype). vw_silv_eligible_invoice has one row per brnz_subs_invoice invoice, and its fee-only test asks whether any own line is an enrolment or application fee and every other own line is tax, which a split does not change. The concession is chosen among the item codes on the segment invoice's concession lines, so a split code is one concession, and an unknown code raises one CONCESSION_NOT_IN_REFERENCE row per contact-year and code. DOUBLE_PAYMENT asks whether Corporate and another method both settle the invoice. The readmission fee check asks whether any own line is a readmission fee. INVOICE_NO_EVENT and EVENT_MATCHES_MULTIPLE_INVOICES are raised once per eligible invoice. None of these readers needs to change, and MOD-020 retests them at the new grain. Only the payment-line fallback in usp_load_silv_member_year_attributes summed a transaction-level value per line, and MOD-020 changes it to count each transaction once. Event amounts read no lines (Q-038).

Adjustment history (REQ-019, RULE-112 to RULE-118): every write to silv_daily_count_detail for a date already marked in etl_daily_count_loaded records, in the same transaction, one silv_daily_count_adjustment row per cell whose figures changed. The row holds new minus old per measure, with a missing cell counting as 0 and an unchanged measure as 0. A date not yet marked loaded is a first load and records nothing. Today is marked loaded by its first load, so every later reload of today records its changes (RULE-114). Every path records under its own run_id: the scheduled run, the first run after deployment, @RebuildFrom and @FullRebuild (RULE-115). For every cell and measure, the figure stored after a run equals the figure before it plus that run's adjustment rows, including for a run that failed part way (RULE-116). Rows are never updated or deleted (RULE-117). Only the seven daily measures are recorded. Segment columns on events and the annual rate base write nothing, and silv_daily_count changes are the sums of the detail changes (RULE-118).

Figures as known at T (REQ-020, ADR-008; Q-049, Q-050, Q-051 answered): fn_silv_daily_count_detail_as_known_at and fn_silv_daily_count_as_known_at return the stored figure minus the changes written strictly after T. written_at and T are both database server local time, so a change written exactly at T is part of the figure at T. A cell removed after T counts as 0 today and so shows its figure at T. A date first loaded after T shows its first-load figures, because no first-load time is tracked. The history starts with the first run after deployment, so for a T before that run the figures are those stored just before it. vw_silv_daily_count_adjustment_review lists one row per adjustment and non-zero measure, keeping the cell's grain columns. Tests use the silver grade 'election' where the spec's AC-020 cells say 'Qualified', which is the gold dim_membership_grade name.
security: No new personal data: contact_no already exists in Phase 1, and no names, emails or bank details are landed. No masking is needed. Every count-only procedure returns aggregates only, with no contact-level columns (RULE-057, RULE-064, RULE-066). The as-known-at functions and the adjustments review view return figures by daily count cell only, with no contact column. etl_daily_count_input_basis holds contact numbers already present in Phase 1 and is internal, so it gets no grant. Grants are scripted by the Developer in src/sql/grants/<MOD>.sql for a human to run. The four new dimensions, the two as-known-at functions and vw_silv_daily_count_adjustment_review get SELECT for the existing reporting role that reads fact_membership_events. The usp_profile_* and usp_report_* procedures get EXECUTE for the analyst role that runs the profiling. Agents hold no grant rights. External sources are read with the project's existing read access and never written.
performance: No volumes are given in the spec. Working estimate: about 140,000 members, so about 140,000 subscription invoices a year from 2022, about one attributes row and one brnz_subs_status row per member per year, and one silv_event_amount row per Join, Renewal and Readmission. Invoice lines are at ledger-distribution grain. Profiling (Q-021) found 458,563 transactions split across 1,015,865 rows, so brnz_subs_invoice_line is expected to hold one to a few million rows. Indexes: brnz_subs_invoice on (account_num, campaign_year) and voucher; brnz_subs_invoice_line clustered on line_id, with a unique index on (recid, postingtype, accountdisplayvalue) (up to about 1 KB per entry, within the nonclustered key limit, ADR-006) and indexes on (accountnum, voucher) and lastsettlevoucher as before; brnz_corporate_subscription on (contact_no, sub_campaign_year); silv_event_amount on (contact_no, amount_campaign_year) and invoice_rec_id; silv_member_year_attributes is clustered on its key. brnz_subs_status is read by its key ([Contact No.], [Campaign Year]) for event amounts and the derived date. No index is added to it, to other Phase 1 tables or to external objects. All loads are set-based full comparisons that write only differences, so the daily cost is dominated by reading the bronze sources. The first invoice line load after MOD-019 soft-deletes the rows landed at the old grain and inserts the source rows once. The daily count correction (ADR-007) adds a fingerprint pass over the four silver inputs on every run, with about one basis row per contact. It then recomputes the daily counts from the earliest changed date, which is usually within the current Campaign Year because backdated events and payments mostly fall there. A changed reference input, or the first run after deployment, recomputes from 2020-10-01 and takes about as long as @FullRebuild. Mike accepts longer runs on those days. The first run's catch-up writes one adjustment row per drifted cell. After that, rows grow with the number of changed cells per run, and the table is kept indefinitely. silv_daily_count_adjustment is clustered on adjustment_id, with the unique index on run and cell and an index on ([date], written_at) for the as-known-at functions. etl_daily_count_input_basis is clustered on its key.

design_elements: Layercake.usp_run_payment_segments runs after Phase 1 (ADR-001), as the last step of Layercake.usp_run_daily_load

Phase 1 procedures unchanged except usp_load_brnz_subs_status, usp_load_silv_member_base (retirement date only, ADR-005), usp_load_silv_data_anomaly (own types only), the silv_payment_events load, usp_load_silv_daily_count (which dates are recomputed and how they are written, ADR-007) and usp_run_daily_load (segment step)
Enrichment procedures update only the new columns
Derived retirement date pattern: only membership_status_id and results split by it change (RULE-102, Q-046)
Invoice line grain pattern: one row per (recid, postingtype, accountdisplayvalue), with the five ledger columns (RULE-104)
ADR-006 invoice line key: line_id primary key and a unique index on the row identity
Payment-line fallback counts each payment transaction once (RULE-013, RULE-105)
DOUBLE_PAYMENT and payer type unaffected by split payment lines (invoice line grain pattern)
Line types serve the eligible-invoice test and readmission fee check only; currency describes no event amount (Q-038)
One mapping row per distinct item code however many lines carry it (invoice line grain pattern)
subs_amount_gbp, invoiced_subtotal_gbp and amount_status on silv_membership_events and fact_membership_events, with the eight unsupplied amount columns dropped (Q-038)
Invoice match in silv_event_amount, for the checks only (Q-042)
Readmission fee check and invoice-level anomalies at the invoice line grain (RULE-105)
A concession split across lines is one concession; an unknown code raises one anomaly (invoice line grain pattern)
Entity descriptions, patterns and known gaps in this design (including Q-038 and Q-040) as source content for the handover pack and the Platform Schema document
Derived retirement date; runbook with no one-off daily rebuild (REQ-018) and with usp_run_daily_load as the only scheduled procedure (REQ-021)

Layercake.usp_load_silv_member_base (retirement_date from the derived date, ADR-005)
Past daily counts take a changed retirement date on the next run with no one-off rebuild (daily count correction pattern, Layercake.usp_load_silv_daily_count)

ADR-007 input comparison against a stored basis
etl_daily_count_pending_rebuild kept as a diagnostic only
Layercake.usp_load_silv_daily_count (writes adjustment rows in the same transaction as each change)

Layercake.usp_run_daily_load (runs usp_run_payment_segments as its last step under the same run_id)

open_questions.question: The dev database could not be queried for this design (schema lookup unavailable), so spec Q-028 is not yet confirmed. The design assumes the following Phase 1 names, which the Developer confirms at the start of MOD-007: silv_membership_events.contact_no, campaign_year, event_type, event_date, event_nk and event_id (with their types); silv_data_anomaly columns anomaly_type, contact_no, anomaly_nk and detail (with no constraint limiting anomaly_type values); silv_member_base as the source of the contact list and first-event year; the object and column holding the Phase 1 paid position; the Full Concession and Partially Paid positions (v1 named Layercake.brnz_subs_status 'Member Invoice Position'); and Layercake.etl_run_log's run id. Are these right?

How are the Phase 1 silv_membership_events, fact_membership_events, silv_payment_events and silv_data_anomaly loaded? Do they rebuild in full each run or apply only changes, and do the anomaly writers delete anomaly types they do not own? What are the procedure names, and how is the Phase 1 run scheduled, so that usp_run_payment_segments can run straight after it? ADR-001 assumes change-only loads that leave other anomaly types alone.
open_questions.answer: Layercake.usp_load_silv_payment_events, called by usp_load_silver, is the only loader of silv_payment_events (MOD-009 answer). The Phase 1 loads apply only differences, and each manages its own transaction and logging (ASM-008). The Phase 1 anomaly load now resolves only its own types (MOD-008 answer). Scheduling: Layercake.usp_run_daily_load runs usp_run_payment_segments as its last step under the same run_id, so nobody schedules a second procedure (Mike, AMD-003, 2026-11-17).

open_questions.question: Spec Q-023 is recorded as answered 'Campaign Year Quarter', but RULE-092, the spec's assumptions, AC-009-03 and AC-009-05 use calendar 1 April to 30 June. Is the free-readmission window the Campaign Year's second quarter, and does it coincide with April to June (does the Campaign Year start on 1 January)? Working assumption: Campaign Year quarter 2 (ADR-004).
open_questions.answer: The free-readmission window is the Campaign Year's second quarter, 1 January to 31 March for a Campaign Year starting 1 October, matching Phase 1's campaign_quarter Q2. It does not coincide with April to June; RULE-092, the spec's assumption and AC-009-05 (now dated 2025-02-14) are corrected to match (Mike, 2026-11-10).

open_questions.question: Subs.vwCorpSubscriptions has no row key. The design assumes (Contact No, Scheme No, Sub Campaign Year) is unique per source row and lands on that key. Can a contact appear twice in the same scheme and year (for example as two subscription users)? If so, which row should bronze keep?

Who supplies the curated item-code to line-type mapping that seeds silv_ref_invoice_line_type (RULE-028, Damian's Story 3 design note)? Working assumption: the seed follows how Subs.usp_Refresh_SubsInvoices classifies item codes, Damian reviews it, and tests use synthetic codes.

Removing silv_payment_events.payment_source drops a column that holds data, which base standards 3.2 says needs a named human's approval. Does Mike approve the drop, given spec Q-024 (no downstream reader) is still open? The down script re-adds the column and restores the previous load procedure, which refills it on the next run.

The spec gives no tie-breaks. To keep results deterministic the design uses: equal trans_dates broken by the higher rec_id (segment invoice and pairing order); equal event dates broken by event_nk; and the lowest scheme_no where a contact has several live corporate subscriptions in one year (corporate_account_ref). Are these acceptable?

The spec maps the standard bronze audit columns _loaded_at, _updated_at, _is_deleted and _deleted_at (as on existing bronze tables), but the project's column-name convention (^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$) rejects a leading underscore. Should the convention in config/project.yaml and PROJECT_STANDARDS.md be widened to allow the existing bronze audit columns (recommended, to match Phase 1 bronze), or should new bronze tables use other names? Until decided, the design keeps the spec's names, described in each bronze entity's text.
open_questions.answer: Approved by Mike by merging RPST PR #6 (2026-10-26): widen the convention, as the Architect recommended. config/project.yaml and PROJECT_STANDARDS.md now allow an optional leading underscore (^_?[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$), matching the Phase 1 bronze tables, and the four standard audit columns (_loaded_at, _updated_at, _is_deleted, _deleted_at) are listed on brnz_subs_invoice, brnz_subs_invoice_line, brnz_corporate_subscription and brnz_concession with the existing bronze types.

open_questions.question: Which Phase 1 objects read Layercake.silv_member_base.retirement_date, and does the derived retirement date change anything beyond Practising / Retired (which membership events exist, their dates, or any difference or reconciliation script)?
open_questions.answer: The derived retirement date replaces silv_member_base.retirement_date for every reader, and it only sets Practising / Retired (membership_status_id). It does not change which membership events exist or their dates: every Phase 1 use in usp_load_silv_membership_events is inside the join that picks the status, and the annual rate base and daily counts use it for status only. No difference or reconciliation script reads silv_member_base.retirement_date; their diagnostic columns keep showing apuk_retirementdate, and their PASS checks are unaffected (Mike, 2026-11-09).

open_questions.question: The daily count design (ADR-007) assumes three things, which the Developer confirms from the Phase 1 code at the start of MOD-022. (a) The handling of @RebuildFrom and @FullRebuild (which dates are recomputed, and clearing their loaded marks) sits in usp_load_silv_daily_count, which usp_load_silver calls with those parameters, so usp_load_silver needs no change. (b) silv_daily_count holds, for each [date], region and grade, the sum of silv_daily_count_detail over country_id, gender_id and membership_status_id. (c) The full list of tables and columns the daily derivation reads, which the input basis must cover; the change note records it. If (a) is wrong, usp_load_silver joins MOD-022's objects. If (b) is wrong, fn_silv_daily_count_as_known_at cannot equal silv_daily_count, and the spec's RULE-120 needs revisiting.
